```{r}
#| label: pressure-sources
#| echo: true
#| output: false
# A box around Mai Ndombe with a margin of 0.5 degrees covers the distance layers, and a box that adds Kinshasa province with a margin of 1.5 degrees covers the routes to Kinshasa and to the markets just outside the province, Mbandaka among them
# GADM version 4.1, level 1 boundaries of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
# https://geodata.ucdavis.edu/gadm/gadm4.1/json/gadm41_COD_1.json.zip
near <- unname(sf::st_bbox(mai_ndombe)) + c(-0.5, -0.5, 0.5, 0.5)
reach <- unname(sf::st_bbox(dplyr::filter(sf::st_read("/vsizip/02.inputs/gadm/raw/gadm41_COD_1.json.zip", quiet = TRUE), NAME_1 %in% c("Mai-Ndombe", "Kinshasa")))) + c(-1.5, -1.5, 1.5, 1.5)
# GADM version 4.1, level 2 boundaries of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
# https://geodata.ucdavis.edu/gadm/gadm4.1/json/gadm41_COD_2.json.zip
fetch("https://geodata.ucdavis.edu/gadm/gadm4.1/json/gadm41_COD_2.json.zip", "02.inputs/gadm/raw/gadm41_COD_2.json.zip")
territories <- sf::st_read("/vsizip/02.inputs/gadm/raw/gadm41_COD_2.json.zip", quiet = TRUE) |> dplyr::filter(NAME_1 == "Mai-Ndombe")
# Modelled gridded population estimates for the Kinshasa, Kongo-Central, Kwango, Kwilu, and Mai-Ndombe provinces in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, version 2.0, WorldPop
# https://data.worldpop.org/repo/wopr/COD/population/v2.0/, https://doi.org/10.5258/SOTON/WP00669
fetch("https://data.worldpop.org/repo/wopr/COD/population/v2.0/COD_population_v2_0_gridded.zip", "02.inputs/worldpop/raw/COD_population_v2_0_gridded.zip")
# Bottom-up gridded population estimates for Maï-Ndombe Province in the Democratic Republic of Congo, version 4.4, WorldPop
# https://data.worldpop.org/repo/wopr/COD/population/v4.4/Province/Mai_Ndombe/, https://doi.org/10.5258/SOTON/WP00867
fetch("https://data.worldpop.org/repo/wopr/COD/population/v4.4/Province/Mai_Ndombe/COD_Mai_Ndombe_province_population_v4.4_gridded.zip", "02.inputs/worldpop/raw/COD_Mai_Ndombe_province_population_v4.4_gridded.zip")
# GRID3 layers are read in pages of 2,000 features, each kept as a file so that a stopped download resumes, and merged when every page is in
fetch_features <- function(service, box, file) if (!file.exists(file)) {
  query <- paste0(service, "/FeatureServer/0/query?where=1%3D1&geometry=", paste(box, collapse = "%2C"), "&geometryType=esriGeometryEnvelope&inSR=4326&spatialRel=esriSpatialRelIntersects&outSR=4326")
  pages <- file.path(sub("\\.gpkg$", "", file), sprintf("page_%04d.geojson", seq_len(ceiling(jsonlite::fromJSON(paste0(query, "&returnCountOnly=true&f=json"))$count / 2000))))
  # The server sometimes answers a page with an error message instead of features, so such a page is deleted and asked for again, up to three times
  purrr::iwalk(pages, \(page, i) for (attempt in 1:3) {
    fetch(paste0(query, "&outFields=*&orderByFields=OBJECTID&resultOffset=", (i - 1L) * 2000L, "&resultRecordCount=2000&f=geojson"), page)
    if (!startsWith(readChar(page, 9), "{\"error\"")) break
    file.remove(page)
    Sys.sleep(30)
  })
  features <- purrr::map(pages, \(page) dplyr::mutate(sf::st_read(page, quiet = TRUE), dplyr::across(!geometry, as.character))) |> dplyr::bind_rows()
  sf::st_write(features, sub("\\.gpkg$", "-part.gpkg", file), delete_dsn = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)
  file.rename(sub("\\.gpkg$", "-part.gpkg", file), file)
}
# GRID3 COD - Settlement Names v9.0, Center for International Earth Science Information Network and GRID3
# https://data.grid3.org/datasets/f4a459a34e43476a9a9671c4095bddd9/about, https://doi.org/10.7916/77t0-h465
fetch_features("https://services3.arcgis.com/BU6Aadhn6tbBEdyk/arcgis/rest/services/GRID3_COD_settlement_names_v9_0", near, "02.inputs/grid3/raw/settlement_names_v9_0.gpkg")
# GRID3 COD - Roads v1.0, Center for International Earth Science Information Network and GRID3
# https://data.grid3.org/datasets/b489c28df02247e3b227dc1adee1dad4/about, https://doi.org/10.7916/00gb-e164
fetch_features("https://services3.arcgis.com/BU6Aadhn6tbBEdyk/arcgis/rest/services/GRID3_COD_roads_v1_0", reach, "02.inputs/grid3/raw/roads_v1_0.gpkg")
# Congo Basin Forest Roads, January 2019 to December 2024, Slagter et al. (2024)
# https://gee-community-catalog.org/projects/forest_roads/, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rse.2024.114380
if (!file.exists("02.inputs/forestroads/raw/forest_roads_2019_2024.geojson")) fetch(ee$FeatureCollection("projects/wurnrt-loggingroads/assets/distribution/forestroads_afr_2019-01_2024-12")$filterBounds(ee$Geometry$Rectangle(reach))$getDownloadURL("geojson"), "02.inputs/forestroads/raw/forest_roads_2019_2024.geojson")
# GRIP4 Global Roads Inventory Project, Africa, Meijer et al. (2018), GLOBIO, PBL Netherlands Environmental Assessment Agency
# https://gee-community-catalog.org/projects/grip/, https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aabd42
if (!file.exists("02.inputs/grip4/raw/grip4_africa.geojson")) fetch(ee$FeatureCollection("projects/sat-io/open-datasets/GRIP4/Africa")$filterBounds(ee$Geometry$Rectangle(reach))$getDownloadURL("geojson"), "02.inputs/grip4/raw/grip4_africa.geojson")
# Bing Maps mined roads, Middle Africa, release of 28 April 2025, Microsoft
# https://github.com/microsoft/RoadDetections, https://usaminedroads.z19.web.core.windows.net/drops/2025.04.28/Middle_Africa.zip
fetch("https://usaminedroads.z19.web.core.windows.net/drops/2025.04.28/Middle_Africa.zip", "02.inputs/msroads/raw/Middle_Africa.zip")
if (!file.exists("02.inputs/msroads/raw/msroads_cod.gpkg")) {
  # Each line holds a country code and one road as GeoJSON, and the roads of the Democratic Republic of the Congo are kept
  lines <- readr::read_tsv(unz("02.inputs/msroads/raw/Middle_Africa.zip", "Middle_Africa.tsv"), col_names = c("iso3", "feature"), col_types = "cc", quote = "") |> dplyr::filter(iso3 == "COD")
  writeLines(lines$feature, "02.inputs/msroads/raw/msroads_cod.geojsonl")
  sf::st_write(sf::st_read("02.inputs/msroads/raw/msroads_cod.geojsonl", quiet = TRUE), "02.inputs/msroads/raw/msroads_cod.gpkg", quiet = TRUE)
}
# Share of Kinshasa's charcoal volume, sold by the wholesalers surveyed, that came from each territory of Mai Ndombe, Figure 9 on page 23 of Dubiez et al. (2021)
# http://agritrop.cirad.fr/600203/1/20220106_Rapport_Filie%CC%80re_bois_e%CC%81nergie_Kinshasa_CIRAD_Vf.pdf
charcoal <- tibble::tribble(~NAME_2, ~share, "Kutu", 11.0, "Oshwe", 4.9, "Inongo", 0.6, "Kwamouth", 0.5)
# The other territories were absent from the figure and take a share of 0
territories <- dplyr::left_join(territories, charcoal, by = "NAME_2") |> dplyr::mutate(share = dplyr::coalesce(share, 0))
```

```{r}
# Distance from non-forest at the start of each period, built at 10 m as VT0007 builds it, where forest in 2021 counts only if the 2016 map was forest too
lc_grid <- ee$data$getAsset("projects/manuscripts-december/assets/deforisk-congo/landcover_2016")$bands[[1]]$grid
landcover <- purrr::map(c(`2016` = 2016L, `2021` = 2021L), \(y) ee$Image(paste0("projects/manuscripts-december/assets/deforisk-congo/landcover_", y)))
nonforest <- list(`2016` = landcover[["2016"]]$neq(5L), `2021` = landcover[["2016"]]$neq(5L)$Or(landcover[["2021"]]$neq(5L)))
made <- c(purrr::map_chr(ee$data$listAssets(list(parent = "projects/manuscripts-december/assets/deforisk-congo"))$assets, "name"), purrr::map_chr(purrr::keep(ee$data$getTaskList(), \(t) t$state %in% c("READY", "RUNNING")), \(t) paste0("projects/manuscripts-december/assets/deforisk-congo/", t$description)))
purrr::iwalk(nonforest, \(nf, y) if (!paste0("projects/manuscripts-december/assets/deforisk-congo/edge_distance_", y) %in% made) ee$batch$Export$image$toAsset(image = nf$fastDistanceTransform(1024L, "pixels", "squared_euclidean")$sqrt()$multiply(lc_grid$affineTransform$scaleX)$round()$toUint16()$updateMask(landcover[["2016"]]$mask()), description = paste0("edge_distance_", y), assetId = paste0("projects/manuscripts-december/assets/deforisk-congo/edge_distance_", y), region = region$bounds(), crs = lc_grid$crsCode, crsTransform = c(lc_grid$affineTransform$scaleX, 0, lc_grid$affineTransform$translateX, 0, lc_grid$affineTransform$scaleY, lc_grid$affineTransform$translateY), maxPixels = 1e11)$start())
```

```{r}
#| label: pressure-layers
#| echo: true
#| output: false
# The 100 m grid nests ten by ten pixels of the 10 m land cover maps from the same origin, and a margin of 500 cells catches features just outside it
grid100 <- terra::rast(xmin = lc_grid$affineTransform$translateX, xmax = lc_grid$affineTransform$translateX + 100 * ceiling(lc_grid$dimensions$width / 10), ymin = lc_grid$affineTransform$translateY - 100 * ceiling(lc_grid$dimensions$height / 10), ymax = lc_grid$affineTransform$translateY, resolution = 100, crs = lc_grid$crsCode)
wide <- terra::extend(grid100, 500)
cell_km2 <- prod(terra::res(grid100)) / 1e6
# A layer is written to a -part.tif file and renamed when complete, so a stopped render builds it again
save_rast <- function(x, file) {
  dir.create(dirname(file), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  terra::writeRaster(x, sub("\\.tif$", "-part.tif", file), overwrite = TRUE, gdal = "COMPRESS=DEFLATE")
  file.rename(sub("\\.tif$", "-part.tif", file), file)
}
# Population density in people per km², from counts summed onto the 100 m cells
# Modelled gridded population estimates for the Kinshasa, Kongo-Central, Kwango, Kwilu, and Mai-Ndombe provinces in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, version 2.0, WorldPop
# https://data.worldpop.org/repo/wopr/COD/population/v2.0/, https://doi.org/10.5258/SOTON/WP00669
if (!file.exists("03.outputs/TIF/population_2018.tif")) save_rast(terra::project(terra::rast("/vsizip/02.inputs/worldpop/raw/COD_population_v2_0_gridded.zip/COD_population_v2_0_gridded/COD_population_v2_0_gridded.tif"), grid100, method = "sum") / cell_km2, "03.outputs/TIF/population_2018.tif")
# Bottom-up gridded population estimates for Maï-Ndombe Province in the Democratic Republic of Congo, version 4.4, WorldPop
# https://data.worldpop.org/repo/wopr/COD/population/v4.4/Province/Mai_Ndombe/, https://doi.org/10.5258/SOTON/WP00867
if (!file.exists("03.outputs/TIF/population_2024.tif")) save_rast(terra::project(terra::rast("/vsizip/02.inputs/worldpop/raw/COD_Mai_Ndombe_province_population_v4.4_gridded.zip/COD_Mai_Ndombe_province_population_v4.4_gridded/COD_Mai_Ndombe_province_population_v4_4_gridded.tif"), grid100, method = "sum") / cell_km2, "03.outputs/TIF/population_2024.tif")
# Distance in metres to the nearest named settlement or camp
# GRID3 COD - Settlement Names v9.0, Center for International Earth Science Information Network and GRID3
# https://data.grid3.org/datasets/f4a459a34e43476a9a9671c4095bddd9/about, https://doi.org/10.7916/77t0-h465
if (!file.exists("03.outputs/TIF/settlement_distance.tif")) save_rast(terra::crop(terra::distance(terra::rasterize(terra::project(terra::vect("02.inputs/grid3/raw/settlement_names_v9_0.gpkg"), lc_grid$crsCode), wide)), grid100), "03.outputs/TIF/settlement_distance.tif")
# Distance in metres to the nearest forest road opened before 2021, the rule of the confirmation test, so one layer serves both periods
# Congo Basin Forest Roads, January 2019 to December 2024, Slagter et al. (2024)
# https://gee-community-catalog.org/projects/forest_roads/, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rse.2024.114380
if (!file.exists("03.outputs/TIF/forest_road_distance.tif")) {
  forest_roads <- terra::vect("02.inputs/forestroads/raw/forest_roads_2019_2024.geojson")
  save_rast(terra::crop(terra::distance(terra::rasterize(terra::project(forest_roads[forest_roads$Year < 2021, ], lc_grid$crsCode), wide, touches = TRUE)), grid100), "03.outputs/TIF/forest_road_distance.tif")
}
# Each territory's share of Kinshasa's charcoal, in per cent
if (!file.exists("03.outputs/TIF/charcoal_share.tif")) save_rast(terra::rasterize(terra::project(terra::vect(territories), lc_grid$crsCode), grid100, field = "share"), "03.outputs/TIF/charcoal_share.tif")
```

```{r}
#| label: travel-time
#| echo: true
#| output: false
# Hours to Kinshasa's urban centre by the fastest route over GRID3 roads and boat routes and the forest roads opened before 2021, on foot elsewhere
# The 100 m grid covers the routes to Kinshasa and shares the origin of the pressure grid
grid_reach <- terra::rast(terra::align(terra::ext(terra::project(terra::vect(terra::ext(reach[1], reach[3], reach[2], reach[4]), crs = "EPSG:4326"), lc_grid$crsCode)), grid100, snap = "out"), resolution = 100, crs = lc_grid$crsCode)
# Global friction surface, walking only, 2019, Malaria Atlas Project, from Weiss et al. (2020)
# https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/projects_malariaatlasproject_assets_accessibility_friction_surface_2019_v5_1_walking_only, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-020-1059-1
walking <- ee$Image("projects/malariaatlasproject/assets/accessibility/friction_surface/2019_v5_1_walking_only")
if (!file.exists("02.inputs/map/raw/friction_walking_2019.tif")) fetch(walking$getDownloadURL(list(region = ee$Geometry$Rectangle(reach), crs = "EPSG:4326", crs_transform = walking$projection()$getInfo()$transform, format = "GEO_TIFF")), "02.inputs/map/raw/friction_walking_2019.tif")
# GHS-SMOD R2023A, degree of urbanisation settlement model, 2020, European Commission Joint Research Centre
# https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/JRC_GHSL_P2023A_GHS_SMOD_V2-0, https://doi.org/10.2905/A0DF7A6F-49DE-46EA-9BDE-563437A6E2BA
if (!file.exists("02.inputs/ghsl/raw/smod_2020.tif")) fetch(ee$ImageCollection("JRC/GHSL/P2023A/GHS_SMOD_V2-0")$filter(ee$Filter$eq("system:index", "2020"))$first()$getDownloadURL(list(region = ee$Geometry$Rectangle(reach), crs = "EPSG:4326", scale = 1000L, format = "GEO_TIFF")), "02.inputs/ghsl/raw/smod_2020.tif")
# Friction in minutes per metre on any grid, the faster of the road and boat network and walking in each cell
# Each GRID3 road and boat route keeps the speed GRID3 estimated for it, in km/h, and a road found only in the other three sources takes the median speed GRID3 gave its roads of class track
friction_on <- function(grid, walk_method) {
  # GRID3 COD - Roads v1.0, Center for International Earth Science Information Network and GRID3
  # https://data.grid3.org/datasets/b489c28df02247e3b227dc1adee1dad4/about, https://doi.org/10.7916/00gb-e164
  roads <- terra::project(terra::vect("02.inputs/grid3/raw/roads_v1_0.gpkg"), lc_grid$crsCode)
  roads$speed <- as.numeric(roads$speed_estimate)
  track <- stats::median(roads$speed[roads$class == "track"], na.rm = TRUE)
  # Congo Basin Forest Roads, January 2019 to December 2024, Slagter et al. (2024), opened before 2021
  # https://gee-community-catalog.org/projects/forest_roads/, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rse.2024.114380
  forest_roads <- terra::vect("02.inputs/forestroads/raw/forest_roads_2019_2024.geojson")
  # GRIP4 Global Roads Inventory Project, Africa, Meijer et al. (2018)
  # https://gee-community-catalog.org/projects/grip/, https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aabd42
  # Bing Maps mined roads, Middle Africa, release of 28 April 2025, Microsoft
  # https://github.com/microsoft/RoadDetections
  others <- list(forest_roads[forest_roads$Year < 2021, ], terra::vect("02.inputs/grip4/raw/grip4_africa.geojson"), terra::vect("02.inputs/msroads/raw/msroads_cod.gpkg"))
  speeds <- c(list(terra::rasterize(roads[!is.na(roads$speed) & roads$speed > 0, ], grid, field = "speed", fun = "max", touches = TRUE)), purrr::map(others, \(v) terra::rasterize(terra::project(v, lc_grid$crsCode), grid, touches = TRUE) * track))
  min(60 / (max(terra::rast(speeds), na.rm = TRUE) * 1000), terra::project(terra::rast("02.inputs/map/raw/friction_walking_2019.tif"), grid, method = walk_method), na.rm = TRUE)
}
graph <- reticulate::import("skimage.graph")
if (!file.exists("03.outputs/TIF/travel_time_kinshasa.tif")) {
  # Kinshasa's urban centre is the largest patch of urban centre cells, class 30, inside Kinshasa province
  # GADM version 4.1, level 1 boundaries of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
  # https://geodata.ucdavis.edu/gadm/gadm4.1/json/gadm41_COD_1.json.zip
  kinshasa <- terra::vect(dplyr::filter(sf::st_read("/vsizip/02.inputs/gadm/raw/gadm41_COD_1.json.zip", quiet = TRUE), NAME_1 == "Kinshasa"))
  urban <- terra::as.polygons(terra::patches(terra::classify(terra::mask(terra::rast("02.inputs/ghsl/raw/smod_2020.tif"), kinshasa), cbind(30, 1), others = NA), directions = 8))
  targets <- terra::rasterize(terra::project(urban[which.max(terra::expanse(urban)), ], lc_grid$crsCode), grid_reach, touches = TRUE)
  costs <- terra::as.matrix(friction_on(grid_reach, "near"), wide = TRUE)
  costs[is.na(costs)] <- Inf
  # The least-cost route from every cell to the urban centre, over eight neighbours with diagonal steps weighted by their length
  mcp <- graph$MCP_Geometric(reticulate::r_to_py(costs)$copy(), fully_connected = TRUE, sampling = terra::res(grid_reach))
  minutes <- reticulate::py_to_r(mcp$find_costs(reticulate::r_to_py(lapply(asplit(which(!is.na(terra::as.matrix(targets, wide = TRUE)), arr.ind = TRUE) - 1L, 1), as.integer)))[[1]])
  minutes[!is.finite(minutes)] <- NA
  save_rast(terra::crop(terra::rast(minutes / 60, extent = terra::ext(grid_reach), crs = lc_grid$crsCode), grid100), "03.outputs/TIF/travel_time_kinshasa.tif")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: roads-merged
#| echo: true
#| output: false
# The four road sources in one layer over the map box, each road keeping its source, class, opening year and the speed the travel time layers gave it
# The sources overlap, so one road can appear up to four times, as it does in the friction surface, where each cell takes the fastest
if (!file.exists("03.outputs/GPKG/roads_merged.gpkg")) {
  box <- sf::st_as_text(sf::st_as_sfc(sf::st_bbox(c(xmin = reach[1], ymin = reach[2], xmax = reach[3], ymax = reach[4]), crs = sf::st_crs(4326))))
  lines_in_box <- \(f) {
    x <- sf::st_read(f, wkt_filter = box, quiet = TRUE)
    x <- sf::st_sf(sf::st_drop_geometry(x), geometry = sf::st_geometry(x))
    x[sf::st_is(x, c("LINESTRING", "MULTILINESTRING")), ]
  }
  # GRID3 COD - Roads v1.0, Center for International Earth Science Information Network and GRID3
  # https://data.grid3.org/datasets/b489c28df02247e3b227dc1adee1dad4/about, https://doi.org/10.7916/00gb-e164
  grid3_file <- "02.inputs/grid3/raw/roads_v1_0.gpkg"
  track <- sf::st_read(grid3_file, query = sprintf("SELECT class, speed_estimate FROM \"%s\"", sf::st_layers(grid3_file)$name[1]), quiet = TRUE) |>
    dplyr::filter(class == "track") |>
    dplyr::pull(speed_estimate) |>
    as.numeric() |>
    stats::median(na.rm = TRUE)
  merged <- rbind(
    dplyr::transmute(lines_in_box(grid3_file), source = "GRID3", class, year = NA_integer_, speed_kmh = as.numeric(speed_estimate)),
    # Congo Basin Forest Roads, January 2019 to December 2024, Slagter et al. (2024); the travel time layers use those opened before 2021
    # https://gee-community-catalog.org/projects/forest_roads/, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rse.2024.114380
    dplyr::transmute(lines_in_box("02.inputs/forestroads/raw/forest_roads_2019_2024.geojson"), source = "Congo Basin Forest Roads", class = "forest road", year = as.integer(Year), speed_kmh = track),
    # GRIP4 Global Roads Inventory Project, Africa, Meijer et al. (2018)
    # https://gee-community-catalog.org/projects/grip/, https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/aabd42
    dplyr::transmute(lines_in_box("02.inputs/grip4/raw/grip4_africa.geojson"), source = "GRIP4", class = paste("road type", GP_RTP), year = NA_integer_, speed_kmh = track),
    # Bing Maps mined roads, Middle Africa, release of 28 April 2025, Microsoft
    # https://github.com/microsoft/RoadDetections, https://usaminedroads.z19.web.core.windows.net/drops/2025.04.28/Middle_Africa.zip
    dplyr::transmute(lines_in_box("02.inputs/msroads/raw/msroads_cod.gpkg"), source = "Microsoft", class = "mined road", year = NA_integer_, speed_kmh = track))
  # Length of each source over the map box and inside Mai Ndombe, in km along the ellipsoid
  # GADM version 4.1, level 1 boundaries of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
  # https://geodata.ucdavis.edu/gadm/gadm4.1/json/gadm41_COD_1.json.zip
  province <- dplyr::filter(sf::st_read("/vsizip/02.inputs/gadm/raw/gadm41_COD_1.json.zip", quiet = TRUE), NAME_1 == "Mai-Ndombe")
  merged$km <- as.numeric(sf::st_length(merged)) / 1000
  inside <- sf::st_intersection(merged, sf::st_geometry(province))
  dplyr::full_join(sf::st_drop_geometry(merged) |> dplyr::summarise(Roads = dplyr::n(), `km in map box` = sum(km), .by = source),
    sf::st_drop_geometry(inside) |> dplyr::mutate(km = as.numeric(sf::st_length(inside)) / 1000) |> dplyr::summarise(`km in Mai Ndombe` = sum(km), .by = source), by = "source") |>
    dplyr::rename(Source = source) |>
    readr::write_excel_csv("03.outputs/TBL/roads-by-source.csv")
  dir.create("03.outputs/GPKG", showWarnings = FALSE)
  sf::st_write(merged, "03.outputs/GPKG/roads_merged-part.gpkg", layer = "roads", quiet = TRUE, delete_dsn = TRUE)
  file.rename("03.outputs/GPKG/roads_merged-part.gpkg", "03.outputs/GPKG/roads_merged.gpkg")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: roads-asset
#| echo: true
#| output: false
# The merged roads are also kept as an Earth Engine asset, so they can be read from any machine
# One export request carries at most 10 MB, and Earth Engine doubles the size of the GeoJSON it is sent, so the roads go up in parts of about 4 MB of GeoJSON, and a later render joins the parts into one asset once every part has finished
roads_dir <- "projects/manuscripts-december/assets/deforisk-congo"
parts_dir <- paste0(roads_dir, "/roads_merged_parts")
listed <- \(dir) c(purrr::map_chr(ee$data$listAssets(list(parent = dir))$assets, "name"), purrr::map_chr(purrr::keep(ee$data$getTaskList(), \(t) t$state %in% c("READY", "RUNNING")), \(t) paste0(dir, "/", t$description)))
if (!paste0(roads_dir, "/roads_merged") %in% listed(roads_dir)) {
  if (!parts_dir %in% listed(roads_dir)) ee$data$createAsset(list(type = "FOLDER"), parts_dir)
  roads <- sf::st_cast(dplyr::select(sf::st_read("03.outputs/GPKG/roads_merged.gpkg", quiet = TRUE), source, class, year, speed_kmh), "MULTILINESTRING")
  # About 22 bytes for each vertex at five decimals, about 1 m, and 120 for each road's fields
  roads$part <- floor(cumsum(22 * tabulate(sf::st_coordinates(roads)[, "L2"], nrow(roads)) + 120) / 3.8e6) + 1
  parts <- sprintf("%s/part_%02d", parts_dir, seq_len(max(roads$part)))
  json <- reticulate::import("json")
  purrr::walk(setdiff(parts, listed(parts_dir)), \(id) {
    collection <- ee$FeatureCollection(json$loads(geojsonsf::sf_geojson(dplyr::select(roads[roads$part == match(id, parts), ], -part), digits = 5)))
    stopifnot(nchar(collection$serialize(), type = "bytes") < 9.5e6)
    ee$batch$Export$table$toAsset(collection = collection, description = basename(id), assetId = id)$start()
  })
  # Every part is listed as an asset only once its export has finished
  finished <- purrr::map_chr(ee$data$listAssets(list(parent = parts_dir))$assets, "name")
  if (all(parts %in% finished)) ee$batch$Export$table$toAsset(collection = ee$FeatureCollection(purrr::map(parts, ee$FeatureCollection))$flatten(), description = "roads_merged", assetId = paste0(roads_dir, "/roads_merged"))$start()
}
```

```{r}
#| label: review-tables
#| echo: true
#| output: false
# Variables of published deforestation risk and pressure models, one row each, read from the full texts on 27 November 2026, each with its quotation and page
model_vars <- readr::read_csv("02.inputs/derived/review-model-variables.csv", col_types = readr::cols(.default = "c"))
# Field measurements of travel for wood, fields and trade in Africa, one row each, read from the full texts on 27 November 2026, each with its quotation and page
field <- readr::read_csv("02.inputs/derived/review-field-distances.csv", col_types = readr::cols(.default = "c")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::everything(), \(x) dplyr::coalesce(x, "")))
# A setting counts as stated when the study printed it, and not when it printed none or nothing
stated <- \(x) {
  x <- tolower(trimws(dplyr::coalesce(x, "")))
  nzchar(x) & !grepl("^(not stated|none|not applicable|no cap)", x)
}
classes <- c(distance_road = "Distance to road", distance_river = "Distance to river", population_density = "Population density",
  distance_settlement = "Distance to settlement", distance_town = "Distance to town", travel_time = "Travel time",
  distance_edge = "Distance to forest edge", population_count = "Population count", distance_market = "Distance to market",
  market_potential = "Market potential")
model_table <- model_vars |>
  dplyr::filter(variable_class %in% names(classes)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Variable = unname(classes[variable_class])) |>
  dplyr::summarise(Studies = dplyr::n_distinct(key),
    `Stated a town size` = dplyr::n_distinct(key[stated(destination_threshold)]),
    `Stated a cap` = dplyr::n_distinct(key[stated(travel_time_cap)]),
    `Stated a decay` = dplyr::n_distinct(key[stated(decay)]), .by = Variable) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(Studies), Variable)
readr::write_excel_csv(model_table, "03.outputs/TBL/tbl-model-variables.csv")
# A value printed as a range, such as 2.0 to 4.8, enters the range at its two ends and the median at its midpoint
ends <- function(v) {
  v <- gsub("[<>]", "", gsub(",", ".", v))
  two <- "(?s)^\\s*(\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)?)\\s*(?:-|to)\\s*(\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)?).*$"
  one <- "(?s)^\\s*(\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)?).*$"
  lo <- suppressWarnings(ifelse(grepl(one, v, perl = TRUE), as.numeric(sub(one, "\\1", v, perl = TRUE)), NA))
  hi <- suppressWarnings(ifelse(grepl(two, v, perl = TRUE), as.numeric(sub(two, "\\2", v, perl = TRUE)), lo))
  tibble::tibble(lo, hi)
}
# Rows of one measure, chosen by question, unit, activity and statistic, with values in metres turned into kilometres
pick <- function(q, unit, act, stats, exclude = "^$", metres = FALSE) {
  d <- dplyr::filter(field, grepl(paste0("^(", q, ")$"), question), grepl(.env$unit, .data$unit, ignore.case = TRUE, perl = TRUE),
    grepl(act, activity, ignore.case = TRUE, perl = TRUE), !grepl(exclude, paste(activity, sample), ignore.case = TRUE, perl = TRUE),
    Reduce(`|`, lapply(stats, \(s) startsWith(statistic, s))))
  f <- if (metres) ifelse(grepl("^m\\b", d$unit, perl = TRUE), 0.001, 1) else 1
  dplyr::bind_cols(dplyr::select(d, key), ends(d$value) * f) |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(lo))
}
central <- c("mean", "median", "mode", "single")
# Every distance keeps one decimal, because 0.5 km matters to a person carrying wood, timber or water, and is rounded down
fmt <- \(x) formatC(floor(x * 10 + 1e-9) / 10, format = "f", digits = 1, big.mark = ",")
measure <- \(d, name, lo = d$lo, hi = d$hi, mid = (d$lo + d$hi) / 2) tibble::tibble(Measure = name, Values = nrow(d),
  Studies = dplyr::n_distinct(d$key), Range = paste(fmt(min(lo)), "to", fmt(max(hi))), Median = fmt(stats::median(mid)))
# Supply distances around towns are grouped by the town's population, read from the size the study printed
supply <- dplyr::filter(field, question == "2", unit == "km", !grepl("felling|kiln|walk|carried|distance from city centre", activity, ignore.case = TRUE)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(size = gsub(",", "", settlement_size),
    size = suppressWarnings(dplyr::case_when(
      grepl("\\d\\s*(or \\d+ )?million", size, perl = TRUE) ~ as.numeric(sub("^.*?(\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)?)\\s*(?:or \\d+ )?million.*$", "\\1", size, perl = TRUE)) * 1e6,
      grepl("\\d{4,}", size) ~ as.numeric(sub("^.*?(\\d{4,}).*$", "\\1", size, perl = TRUE)))),
    mid = rowMeans(ends(value))) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(size), !is.na(mid))
by_size <- \(from, to, name) {
  d <- dplyr::filter(supply, size >= from, size < to)
  measure(d, name, lo = d$mid, hi = d$mid, mid = d$mid)
}
# Wood use per person, turned into kg per day from values per week and per year
rural <- dplyr::filter(field, question == "5", grepl("^kg per person per (day|week|year)", unit), !grepl("equivalent|sack", unit),
    grepl("rural|village", paste(settlement_type, settlement_size, place), ignore.case = TRUE)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(use = rowMeans(ends(value)) / dplyr::case_when(grepl("week", unit) ~ 7, grepl("year", unit) ~ 365, .default = 1)) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(use))
field_table <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  measure(pick("1", "^(km|m)\\b", "distance|walk", central, "cited|round trip|stockpost|depletion|radius", metres = TRUE), "Walk to collect wood, km"),
  measure(pick("1", "^h per trip|^h$", "hour|time", c(central, "range"), "walking time village"), "Time per wood collection trip, h"),
  measure(pick("3", "^(km|m)\\b", "field|fallow|farming|cassava", c(central, "maximum", "minimum", "range", "mode"), "city", metres = TRUE), "Home to field, km"),
  measure(pick("4", "^km per", "carrying distance|bicycle travel", c(central, "range", "maximum")), "Daily carrying distance per adult, km"),
  measure(pick("3", "^km$", "market", c(central, "maximum", "minimum", "range")), "Village to market, km"),
  measure(pick("4", "^km", "hunt|snare|expedition|catchment|forest|camp", c(central, "maximum", "range"), "area|road or river"), "Village to hunting ground, km"),
  by_size(5e6, Inf, "Wood supply distance, cities of 5 million or more, km"),
  by_size(1e6, 5e6, "Wood supply distance, cities of 1 to 5 million, km"),
  by_size(0, 1e6, "Wood supply distance, towns under 1 million, km"),
  measure(rural, "Rural wood use, kg per person per day", lo = rural$use, hi = rural$use, mid = rural$use))
readr::write_excel_csv(field_table, "03.outputs/TBL/tbl-field-distances.csv")
```

```{r}
#| label: market-access
#| echo: true
#| output: false
# Market access sums, over every settlement a cell reaches within 12 hours, the settlement's population raised to 0.55 times its travel time in hours raised to -1.25
# Both exponents are those fitted to the wood energy flows of Bamako's villages by Gazull et al. (2011), Table 2
# The 1 km grid is the resolution of Weiss et al. (2018) and shares the origin of the 100 m grid
grid1k <- terra::aggregate(grid_reach, 10)
gt1k <- c(1000, 0, terra::xmin(grid1k), 0, -1000, terra::ymax(grid1k))
# High Resolution Settlement Layer, population, Facebook Connectivity Lab and CIESIN, served by the Earth Engine community catalog
# https://gee-community-catalog.org/projects/hrsl/, https://dataforgood.fb.com/tools/population-density-maps/
if (!file.exists("02.inputs/hrsl/raw/hrsl_1km.tif")) {
  hrsl <- ee$ImageCollection("projects/sat-io/open-datasets/hrsl/hrslpop")$filterBounds(ee$Geometry$Rectangle(reach))
  people <- hrsl$mosaic()$unmask(0)$setDefaultProjection(hrsl$first()$projection())$reduceResolution(ee$Reducer$sum()$unweighted(), maxPixels = 4000L)$reproject(crs = lc_grid$crsCode, crsTransform = gt1k)
  # Earth Engine sums the 30 m cells onto 1 km only for small areas at a time, so the box is read in 16 tiles
  tiles <- tidyr::expand_grid(i = 0:3, j = 0:3) |> dplyr::mutate(file = sprintf("02.inputs/hrsl/raw/tiles/hrsl_%d%d.tif", i, j))
  step <- c(diff(reach[c(1, 3)]), diff(reach[c(2, 4)])) / 4
  # Earth Engine sometimes refuses a tile and serves it on a later request, so each tile is asked for up to three times
  purrr::pwalk(tiles, \(i, j, file) for (attempt in 1:3) {
    got <- try(fetch(people$getDownloadURL(list(region = ee$Geometry$Rectangle(c(reach[1] + i * step[1], reach[2] + j * step[2], reach[1] + (i + 1) * step[1], reach[2] + (j + 1) * step[2])), crs = lc_grid$crsCode, crs_transform = gt1k, format = "GEO_TIFF")), file))
    if (!inherits(got, "try-error")) break
    Sys.sleep(60)
  })
  save_rast(terra::crop(terra::extend(terra::mosaic(terra::sprc(purrr::map(tiles$file, terra::rast)), fun = "max"), grid1k), grid1k), "02.inputs/hrsl/raw/hrsl_1km.tif")
}
if (!file.exists("03.outputs/TIF/market_access.tif")) {
  # A settlement is a group of touching inhabited 1 km cells inside the Democratic Republic of the Congo, so Brazzaville is left out
  # GADM version 4.1, level 1 boundaries of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
  # https://geodata.ucdavis.edu/gadm/gadm4.1/json/gadm41_COD_1.json.zip
  pop1k <- terra::mask(terra::rast("02.inputs/hrsl/raw/hrsl_1km.tif"), terra::project(terra::vect(sf::st_read("/vsizip/02.inputs/gadm/raw/gadm41_COD_1.json.zip", quiet = TRUE)), lc_grid$crsCode))
  settlement <- terra::patches(terra::ifel(pop1k > 0, 1, NA), directions = 8)
  towns <- tibble::tibble(id = terra::values(settlement)[, 1], people = terra::values(pop1k)[, 1], row = terra::rowFromCell(pop1k, seq_len(terra::ncell(pop1k))) - 1L, col = terra::colFromCell(pop1k, seq_len(terra::ncell(pop1k))) - 1L) |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(id)) |>
    dplyr::group_by(id) |>
    dplyr::summarise(people = sum(people), starts = list(purrr::map2(as.integer(row), as.integer(col), c)))
  costs <- terra::as.matrix(friction_on(grid1k, "average"), wide = TRUE)
  costs[is.na(costs)] <- Inf
  mcp <- graph$MCP_Geometric(reticulate::r_to_py(costs)$copy(), fully_connected = TRUE, sampling = terra::res(grid1k))
  # A settlement's own cells count as half an hour away, so that no settlement weighs without limit
  access <- 0
  for (k in seq_len(nrow(towns))) {
    hours <- reticulate::py_to_r(mcp$find_costs(towns$starts[[k]], max_cumulative_cost = 720)[[1]]) / 60
    access <- access + ifelse(is.finite(hours) & hours <= 12, towns$people[k]^0.55 * pmax(hours, 0.5)^-1.25, 0)
  }
  save_rast(terra::rast(access, extent = terra::ext(grid1k), crs = lc_grid$crsCode), "03.outputs/TIF/market_access_1km.tif")
  save_rast(terra::resample(terra::rast("03.outputs/TIF/market_access_1km.tif"), grid100, method = "bilinear"), "03.outputs/TIF/market_access.tif")
}
```

## Benchmark comparison

Placeholder. The comparison with Verra's deforestation risk maps for Mai Ndombe and Equateur provinces [@verra2026jurisdictional] is waiting on access to the maps and on Verra's terms for their published use. In the meantime, the national forest reference emission level of the Democratic Republic of the Congo is being considered as a benchmark [@unfccc2018report]. Its deforestation areas for 2000 to 2014 came from reference samples [@unfccc2018report]. A global forest change dataset, such as that of @Hansen_2013, is being considered as a second benchmark.
